content: coffee A controlled explosion on a film set near London's O2 arena ignited a fire that destroyed a van and damaged a car and a lorry, prompting the London fire brigade to respond to an open‑air yard in Dock Road, Silvertown just before 8 p.m. on Saturday. About twenty‑five firefighters brought the blaze under control in just over an hour, with no injuries reported. The fire is believed to have stemmed from a pre‑planned filming activity at the site, which lies close to the O2 venue that will host concerts by Niall Horan and Texas the following week. The brigade later posted on X that the fire in the Silvertown yard is now under control, noting that one vehicle was destroyed and most of a car and lorry were harmed, while confirming no injuries. They added that the blaze originated from a controlled explosion on the film set that escaped control, that crews extinguished it swiftly, and that personnel would stay on scene for the rest of the evening. The yard is also situated near London’s cable‑car crossing over the River Thames, and a Metropolitan Police spokesman said they are aware of reports of explosions heard near the O2 in Greenwich.
